initial_plan.question_answerability: partly: the file has motorist-death outcomes and crash records but no miles driven, so it cannot estimate risk per mile; it can show the share of reported crashes involving at least one motorist death as an explicitly limited crash-level proxy.
initial_plan.metric: percentage of eligible crash rows with number_of_motorist_killed greater than zero, by crash year
initial_plan.denominator: number of eligible police-reported crash rows in that year
initial_plan.population: police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes with crash_date in 2013–2025 and a nonmissing number_of_motorist_killed value
filters: crash_date is in calendar years 2013 through 2025
exclude rows with missing number_of_motorist_killed from numerator and denominator
initial_plan.years: 2013–2025 inclusive; data checks will identify years absent or present only in part

data_check_decisions.facts: check_2.csv shows zero rows missing crash_date in the file; each year 2013–2025 has complete Jan 1–Dec 31 date coverage; number_of_motorist_killed is missing on zero candidate rows in every year. Eligible rows therefore equal candidate dated rows: 203,742 (2013), 206,046 (2014), 217,708 (2015), 229,833 (2016), 231,007 (2017), 231,564 (2018), 211,486 (2019), 112,918 (2020), 110,558 (2021), 103,887 (2022), 96,607 (2023), 91,316 (2024), and 85,546 (2025).
data_check_decisions.meaning_and_decisions: No rows are lost to missing crash_date or missing motorist-death values in the planned years. Keep all dated crash rows; the initial rule to exclude missing motorist-death rows has no effect. Every planned year is a full calendar year, so no year is excluded for partial coverage. Annual crash-row denominators vary substantially, which must be considered when comparing annual shares; the file has no miles-driven exposure.

final_plan.question_answerability: partly: the data cannot answer whether the risk per mile driven declined because it contains no vehicle-miles-traveled or other driving-exposure denominator. It can describe the share of recorded crashes involving at least one motorist death.
final_plan.metric: 100 × count of eligible crash rows with number_of_motorist_killed greater than zero divided by eligible crash-row count, by crash year
final_plan.denominator: eligible police-reported crash rows for that year (all have a nonmissing number_of_motorist_killed value)
final_plan.population: all police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes dated in 2013–2025 inclusive; one crash row per record
filters: retain rows with nonmissing number_of_motorist_killed; the data check found no such missing rows
final_plan.years: full calendar years 2013–2025, as date coverage is complete in each
final_plan.limitations: This crash-level share does not measure risk per mile driven because no driving-mile exposure is available; it gives equal weight to each crash row and marks whether at least one motorist was killed in that crash. Annual reported-crash denominators rise from 203,742 in 2013 to 231,564 in 2018, then reach 85,546 in 2025, so annual shares describe the composition of recorded crash rows, not individual driving exposure or population risk.
